dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies, state and local governments, Indian Tribes, and communities near abandoned mine sites.
dimensions.evidence: coordinate between the headquarters of the Environmental Protection Agency, Regional Offices, and stakeholders on cleanup actions

dimensions.assessment: Directs administrative coordination, priority lists, and interagency planning rather than altering private legal rights directly.
dimensions.evidence: establish within the Environmental Protection Agency the Office of Mountains, Deserts, and Plains

dimensions.assessment: Requires projected appropriations for interagency plans on Navajo Nation sites, but states the office provides no new regulatory authority or funding appropriations on its own.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this section-- (1) provides the Administrator with new regulatory authority not already established in law

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new organizational office within the EPA and mandates reporting and priority list creation.
dimensions.evidence: There is established within the office of the Environmental Protection Agency that administers solid waste programs the Office of Mountains, Deserts, and Plains.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing annual reporting duties and decennial interagency plans.
dimensions.evidence: Annually, the Administrator shall identify covered mine sites that are prioritized for cleanup actions

importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a new Office within the EPA to coordinate cleanup actions at covered mine sites and requires periodic reports and interagency plans, without granting new regulatory authority.
